title: region-fail-open-admission-control-and-dependency-latency-simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a deterministic chaos harness that simulates combined failure modes: region network partition (control plane reachable, data plane egress cut), GPU pool exhaustion in a single region, and downstream dependency blackholes (KV store and model-mirroring service). The goal is to validate admission control behavior, early-fail (fail-open vs fail-closed) decisioning, circuit-breaker tuning, and load-shedding policies so that regional outages degrade gracefully and SLOs are preserved for tiered customers. Deliverables: (1) repeatable harness that can run in staging and on a dedicated chaos environment; (2) a set of regression tests and traffic profiles that reproduce the incident class observed in incident-2025-11-17; (3) recommendations and config changes for admission-control thresholds, circuit-breaker backoff, and fallback routing to replica regions/cheaper quantized model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can inject: (a) region egress blackhole, (b) GPU pool saturated with synthetic long-running inferences, (c) downstream kv-store 95th-percentile latency spikes and 500s.
Runbook scripts produce consistent metrics: circuit-breaker trip counts, shed-rate, per-client 95th/99th latency, and request error budgets consumed.
A/B test shows admission-control early-503 reduces p95 latency for P1 customers by >=30% compared to unthrottled tail-surge under same injected conditions.
Config changes (proposed) include concrete threshold values and are validated in staging with no regressions to normal traffic for 72 hours post-test.
Artifact links (PRs, dashboards, runbooks) are documented in the ticket and reviewed by PM and SRE.
Safety: chaos runs include an automated abort if platform-wide SLI delta > configured safety window to avoid cross-team impact.
steps: Provision chaos namespace in staging (k8s labels: chaos=true) and reserve a dedicated GPU pool of size 8 for harness runs.
Deploy the harness microservice (chaos-injector) that can toggle iptables egress rules, inject process CPU pressure on model-serving pods, and stub kv-service responses.

Generate synthetic traffic using the compare-traffic tool with two profiles: (A) default traffic mix; (B) high-context long-seq generation (tail-heavy). Use token distributions matching production trace sample from 2026-02.

Run baseline 30m with no injection. Record metrics. Then run scenario matrix: (1) region-egress only, (2) gpu-saturation only, (3) kv-latency only, (4) combined triple-failure. Each scenario runs 20m followed by 10m cool-down.
Collect logs, traces, and dump KV cache hit ratios, batching statistics, and kernel selection counters after each scenario.
Perform A/B where group A uses current admission control, group B uses proposed early-fail 503 with client-visible status.explain header. Compare per-tenant SLOs.
Submit PRs with config changes and gate via canary release to 10% traffic in staging before wider rollout.
metrics_to_record: request error rate (4xx/5xx) by cause (admission control, model-error, kv-timeout)
shed-rate (requests dropped by admission control) and queue depth
allocated GPU utilization and running long-job count
cache hit ratio (prefix/KV) and batching efficiency (tokens/request)
slo burn rate for P0/P1/P2 customers during and after injection
comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem review of incident-2025-11-17. Scope: combine region partition + gpu-pool starvation + kv blackhole. Initial spike hypothesis drafted.

2026-03-04 Ethan Morales: Prototype chaos-injector that flips egress via iptables and pauses wordpiece tokenizer inside serving worker. Local replays show sustained p99 increases in staging when KV delayed.

2026-03-06 SRE Review (Jordan Kim): Recommended adding a safety abort threshold and limiting chaos runs to the dedicated chaos namespace to avoid control-plane alarms. Suggested collecting downstream retries per-call.
2026-03-09 Design feedback (Marta Li): Request to expose a client-visible reason code when we early-503 so product UX can show fallback messaging. Added header plan: X-Redwood-FailReason.

2026-03-11 QA (Lina Rossi): Smoke tests pass for injection toggles. Observed that current circuit-breaker backoff (exp base 2, max 60s) allows oscillation; proposed cap at 30s and jitter to avoid synchronized reopen storms.

2026-03-12 Run #1 (combined): Observed admission-control shed-rate at peak 42% with P1 customers experiencing 12% higher error budget burn than baseline. Action: reduce global shed threshold for P1 from 80qps to 60qps and route to replica region earlier.
2026-03-13 PR review (runtime change): PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2187 contains circuit-breaker telemetry and config knobs. Waiting on SRE sign-off for canary.
2026-03-14 Next: finalize canary config, add automated regression test in CI that replays recorded scenario and asserts no more than 10% p95 delta for P1 in steady state.
notes: Risk: running combined chaos in shared staging could surface unrelated infra bugs. Mitigation: dedicate chaos namespace and throttle frequency.
Decision trade-off: early-503 vs queueing longer. Early-503 improves p95 but increases 4xx surface; will use tiered policy (P0: queue, P1: early-503 with fallback, P2: best-effort).

Success criteria: we can run 3 consecutive combined-scenario runs with consistent metric behavior and a validated config change that reduces P1 p95 during injected incidents by >=30% compared to baseline.
